description: Whole fixture machines in; the canonical SavestatePlacement serialization (atlas.contract.savestate_placement_contract) out, asserted with exact equality: dir, root_kind, needs, fallback_dir, physical_dir, file_set incl. completeness, and caveat codes + data. There is no granularity field and its absence is contractual — no core writes a savestate, so no rule card can ever state one. Layout facts are sourced from RetroArch runloop.c/configuration.c/config.def.h/core_info.c at the pinned revision; see docs/research/retrodeck-save-placement.md §18.

vectors.name: retrodeck-states-flat
vectors.rationale: The flat layout: savestate_directory set, savestates_in_content_dir off and both sort flags off, so neither append runs (runloop.c:8861-8874). States land flat in the configured root, and the .state lying there is observed rather than assumed.

vectors.name: retrodeck-states-sorted-by-content
vectors.rationale: sort_savestates_by_content_enable appends the ROM's parent directory name (runloop.c:8861-8866). Every slot spelling RetroArch writes is observed at once: the base .state, the numbered .state1 (runloop.c:8202-8203), the .state.auto of a negative slot (:8198) and the thumbnail written beside a state (task_screenshot.c:476-485). The .srm and .ldci sharing the directory are not savestates and the narrower glob does not reach them — nor is the .replay of a recorded input movie, which RetroArch puts in this very directory (runloop.c:8923, :8950) and which answers a different question.

vectors.name: retrodeck-states-sorted-by-core
vectors.rationale: sort_savestates_enable appends library_name (runloop.c:8869-8874), read live from the core binary — mGBA, not the .so name.

vectors.rationale: RetroArch writes every savestate below a directory its own configuration names, so a working folder given to the savestate question is ignored: the answer is byte for byte the one without it (retrodeck-states-sorted-by-core).

vectors.name: retrodeck-states-sort-by-core-without-a-core
vectors.rationale: Sorting by core with no core named leaves the <library_name> hole for the caller to fill — a hole, never a guessed directory.

vectors.name: retrodeck-states-in-content-dir
vectors.rationale: savestates_in_content_dir roots the states at the ROM's own directory (runloop.c:8799-8804). This is where the two families' file sets part company: a savefile observation there has to state the whole <stem>.* sweep because the core's extensions are unknown, while <stem>.state* names exactly RetroArch's own artifacts — the ROM, its cover art and its .srm all share the stem and none of them is matched.

vectors.name: retrodeck-states-key-absent-is-not-the-saves-root
vectors.rationale: An absent savestate_directory resolves to RetroArch's platform default — 'states' under the config tree (platform_unix.c:2135-2136) — and emphatically not to the configured saves root, which this cfg sets to somewhere else entirely.

vectors.name: bare-native-states-upstream-defaults-sort-by-core
vectors.rationale: A bare install carries RetroArch's compile-time defaults, where DEFAULT_SORT_SAVESTATES_ENABLE is true (config.def.h:983) exactly as its savefile twin is — so an unconfigured install sorts states into per-library_name subdirectories of the platform default root.

vectors.name: retrodeck-states-blank-in-an-override-keeps-the-root
vectors.rationale: savestate_directory passes handle_setting=false in the settings table (configuration.c:1710), the same as savefile_directory (:1709) — so the generic path loop skips it and only the block that demands path_is_directory sets it (:6935-6960). A blank value fails that test, sets nothing, and the global cfg's root stands.

vectors.name: retrodeck-states-default-resets-to-the-platform-root
vectors.rationale: The literal "default" resets the setting to the platform default unconditionally (configuration.c:6939-6940) — the one spelling that does not mean "keep what stands", which blank does.

vectors.name: retrodeck-states-root-is-not-a-directory
vectors.rationale: A configured root RetroArch's path_is_directory refuses sets nothing, so the platform default stands and the caveat names the layer to fix.

vectors.name: retrodeck-states-dropped-line-is-stated
vectors.rationale: A line whose key runs into the '=' is dropped by RetroArch's parser (config_file.c:596-623), so the states root is not what the file appears to say. The dropped line is stated because it aims at one of this family's own keys.

vectors.name: retrodeck-states-sandbox-path-untranslated
vectors.rationale: A root that exists only inside the sandbox has no host location, so atlas states where the emulator writes and performs no observation there — an empty file set would be a claim about a directory nobody read. Whether RetroArch sees a folder under the sandbox's private /run/user cannot be told either, so save-directory-visibility-unestablished rides beside it (#641).

vectors.name: retrodeck-states-sorted-dir-missing
vectors.rationale: A sorted directory that does not exist yet is a conditional result: RetroArch creates it and silently reverts to the unsorted root when creation fails (runloop.c:8878-8887), so the fallback is structural rather than prose.

vectors.name: retrodeck-states-dir-unlistable
vectors.rationale: A states directory that cannot be listed makes the set unknown, never empty — 'no states here' and 'atlas could not look' are opposite instructions to a client restoring a save.

vectors.name: retrodeck-states-through-a-symlink
vectors.rationale: RetroDECK's dir_prep pattern: the emulator-side directory and the physical one are two truthful answers to different questions, and a state placement reports both.

vectors.name: retrodeck-states-core-declares-no-savestate-support
vectors.rationale: savestate = "false" in a core .info sets CORE_INFO_SAVESTATE_DISABLED (core_info.c:1841-1860) and RetroArch checks that level before offering a state at all (:2899-2937). 68 of the 292 .info files a stock RetroDECK ships declare it, so the directory alone would read as a promise.

vectors.name: retrodeck-entry-state-location
vectors.rationale: The catalogue entry route answers for savestates the way it does for saves: the entry carries its own core, so library_name is resolved without the caller naming one.

vectors.name: retrodeck-entry-state-location-standalone-is-unresolved
vectors.rationale: A standalone entry refuses the state question for exactly the reason it refuses the save one: nothing here reads that emulator's own config. A typed domain outcome, never an exception.

vectors.name: two-arrangements-answer-the-state-question-each
vectors.rationale: The aggregate fans the state question out the way it fans out the save one: two arrangements, two true answers, neither one chosen. The native install's states are sorted by core because its defaults are RetroArch's own; RetroDECK's are flat because its cfg says so.

vectors.name: emudeck-states-under-the-retroarch-flatpak-config-tree
vectors.rationale: EmuDeck writes all four savestate keys (RetroArch_maincfg.sh:3053, :3057, :3091-3092), and unlike its saves root — derived from savesPath — its savestate_directory is a fixed path under the RetroArch Flatpak's own config tree. atlas reads what the cfg says either way.

vectors.name: retrodeck-states-an-appended-config-moves-the-state-directory
vectors.rationale: The savestate quartet goes through the same chain: the appended file's savestate_directory and its sort flag are the boot read and nothing overrides them, so states land flat in the appended root.

vectors.name: retrodeck-states-a-directory-in-another-apps-tree-is-refused-in-the-sandbox
vectors.rationale: retroarch.cfg names a savestate directory inside another Flatpak app's ~/.var/app tree. The RetroDECK sandbox masks it, so RetroArch's directory test fails inside it (configuration.c:6941-6959) and the platform default stands, with invalid-save-directory naming the global layer (#641).

vectors.name: native-a-relative-savestate-folder-is-opened-from-the-callers-cwd
vectors.rationale: savestate_directory takes the same read as its savefile twin (configuration.c:6935-6960), so a relative value is opened from the launch's working directory (file_path.c:1066-1101). Joined to the caller's cwd it passes the directory test and is read: the content's states lying there are listed.

vectors.name: native-a-relative-savestate-folder-without-a-cwd-is-the-cwd-template
vectors.rationale: Without cwd a relative savestate_directory is the <cwd> template with the cwd hole and save-dir-launch-dependent, its directory test left to the launch and nothing read below it.
